events.title: A New York jury finds Trump guilty on 34 felony counts
events.mechanism: A criminal verdict is a major campaign development with legal, reputational, mobilization, and fundraising implications.

claims.text: The jury returned guilty verdicts on 34 counts of falsifying business records in the first degree.

events.competingExplanation: Jury deliberation and public anticipation preceded the bracket; legal reactions and campaign mobilization overlap the window.
events.editorialNotes: The cutoff is an upper bound, not the exact verdict instant.

events.title: A gunman shoots Trump at a Pennsylvania rally; he survives
events.mechanism: A rally shooting is a highly salient campaign event with possible sympathy, security, turnout, and opponent effects.

claims.text: The July 13 Butler rally shooting occurred and Trump survived.

events.competingExplanation: The cutoff follows the shooting and live reporting; Biden-candidacy uncertainty and the approaching Republican convention overlap the broader period.
events.editorialNotes: Repeated Butler card after Biden #001; different contract perspective does not eliminate answer-recall risk.

events.title: Robert F. Kennedy Jr. suspends his campaign and says he will support Trump
events.mechanism: A rival's suspension and support announcement changes the public campaign field while leaving ballot and state-specific details in view.

claims.text: Kennedy announced that he was suspending rather than terminating his campaign and would support Trump in the relevant battleground context.

events.competingExplanation: The decision was discussed before the speech; the Democratic convention's end and later campaign activity overlap the response period.
events.editorialNotes: The negative or surprising measured response, if later calculated by an authorized integration, must not be rewritten.

events.title: Harris and Trump meet for their first presidential debate
events.mechanism: A nationally televised debate provides a long public test of the candidates and can update expectations throughout the broadcast.

claims.text: Harris and Trump participated in their first presidential debate together in Philadelphia.

events.competingExplanation: Information arrived during the broadcast; post-debate commentary, endorsements, and other campaign activity overlap the response windows.
events.editorialNotes: Corrected from the old transcript-page publication anchor. Approximate broadcast end is an upper bound; ABC page modification is not backdated.

events.title: The final Iowa Poll reports Harris ahead of Trump, 47% to 44%
events.mechanism: A late state poll can change campaign narratives, although a state survey is not a national forecast and reported uncertainty matters.

claims.text: The Des Moines Register/Mediacom poll surveyed 808 likely voters and reported Harris 47% and Trump 44%, within a 3.4-point margin of error.

events.competingExplanation: The Register page was blocked during capture; the poll was within its margin of error and the delayed window reaches election-night information.
events.editorialNotes: The first-public UTC minute remains unknown; Reuters' displayed clock timezone was not converted.
